one_liner: Pure-Go (CGO=0) scikit-image-style image library; first-party table shows RGB to HSV and box blur 2-5x faster than float64 scikit-image, far slower than OpenCV.
what_it_does: A cgo-free Go image-processing package modelled on scikit-image: colour (Grayscale, RGBToHSV/HSVToRGB, Otsu), filters (BoxBlur, GaussianBlur, Median, UnsharpMask), edges (Sobel, Scharr, Prewitt, Laplacian, Canny), grayscale morphology, geometry (flip, rotate, crop, affine Warp, EXIF orientation) and Resize, plus decoding of eight formats and a DecodePartial for files still arriving. Every op takes an image.Image and returns a freshly allocated *image.RGBA without mutating the input, so it is a Go API, not a drop-in for numpy/skimage or OpenCV calls. Resize delegates to the go-gfx/gfx resample package; the catalogued numbers cover none of the resampling paths.
how_it_is_fast: The wins come from algorithm and data layout, not vector code: RGBToHSV is one fused scalar per-pixel pass (via go-gfx/gfx/color.SRGBToHSV) instead of scikit-image's chain of float64 numpy temporaries, and BoxBlur is a separable running-window sum (O(1) per pixel in the radius) with a float64 intermediate plane. The only go-asmgen SIMD kernel the current code calls is a float64 axpy (SSE2 on amd64, NEON FMLA on arm64, z/vector on s390x) used by the separable Gaussian; morphology is a scalar van Herk / Gil-Werman running min/max on bytes. Separable passes fan rows or columns out over GOMAXPROCS goroutines above 16,384 pixels; RGBToHSV has no such tiling.
when_to_use: Go services or CLIs that must build with CGO_ENABLED=0 (static binaries, cross-compiling to arm64, s390x, riscv64, loong64 or ppc64le) and need blur, edge, morphology or HSV ops without libvips, ImageMagick or OpenCV.

Batch filtering of large images (1024x1024 and up) on many-core machines, where the goroutine tiling gave 4.2-10.3x over single-threaded scikit-image in the author's 16-core table for box blur, Gaussian, Sobel and morphology.
Porting a scikit-image pipeline to Go when matching its semantics matters: box blur, morphology, Otsu and Rotate/Warp are written and tested against scipy/skimage references.
Byte-quantized HSV for thresholding or colour keying inside an RGBA pipeline, where 1.4-degree hue steps are acceptable.
when_not_to_use: Raw throughput: in the same single-thread table OpenCV (uint8 in, uint8 out) is about 24x faster on RGB to HSV, 15-30x on box blur, 6-8x on Gaussian and 7-8x on Sobel (derived from page data). If cgo is acceptable, OpenCV (or libvips) wins every row.
Small-radius morphology, Rotate90, Crop or Otsu on one thread, where the table shows go-images at 0.24-0.93x of scikit-image.

Memory-constrained 4096x4096 work: every call allocates a new RGBA output, BoxBlur allocates a width*height*3 float64 plane (about 400 MB at 4096x4096) and GaussianBlur six width*height float64 planes (about 800 MB), derived from the code.
Code that needs float or 16-bit images, or HSV in OpenCV's 0-180 or skimage's float convention: everything is 8-bit RGBA and RGBToHSV packs hue into 0-255.
Resizing benchmarks or resize-heavy workloads chosen on these numbers: the parity table has no resize rows and Resize lives in go-gfx/gfx.

integration.dependencies: github.com/go-gfx/gfx v0.34.0, go-images/gif v0.1.0, go-images/jpeg v0.2.0, go-images/png v0.1.0, sergeymakinen/go-ico v1.0.0, golang.org/x/image v0.46.0 (indirect: ajroetker/go-highway, go-images/jpeg2000, sergeymakinen/go-bmp, tannevaled/gobig2, golang.org/x/sys); no cgo
integration.platforms: any Go target; README targets amd64, arm64, riscv64, loong64, ppc64le, s390x. Gaussian axpy is SIMD on amd64 (SSE2), arm64 (NEON) and s390x; other ops are scalar Go everywhere
integration.thread_safety: Ops are pure functions that never mutate their input and return a new *image.RGBA (README); internally they spawn up to GOMAXPROCS goroutines above 16,384 pixels. Concurrent calls are not otherwise documented.

gotchas: RGBToHSV stores H as round(hue*255/360) in the R byte (about 1.41 degrees per step), S and V as bytes; this is neither skimage's float [0,1] nor OpenCV's 0-180 hue. The correctness gate never checks it: benchmarks/verify/main.go writes hsv.bin but benchmarks/verify.py never reads it (only the internal hsv_parity_test.go compares against the previous Go kernel).

GaussianBlur truncates at ceil(3*sigma) (13 taps at sigma 2 vs scipy's 17) and rounds the horizontal pass to bytes before the vertical pass; verify.py allows 4 levels of difference from skimage although BENCHMARKS.md and the README say within one level.
Erode/Dilate/Open/Close work per channel on RGB, so on a colour image they are not luminance morphology; a grayscale result needs Grayscale first.
Setting GOMAXPROCS (or go test -cpu) changes the internal fan-out; the single-thread numbers in BENCHMARKS.md depend on -cpu=1 collapsing the tiling to one goroutine.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over OpenCV, CompV or DeltaCV (all faster C/C++ RGB to HSV) and FastBoxBlur only when the hard requirement is a cgo-free Go build; on speed alone those win, OpenCV by 15-30x on the measured ops. Against rez, the other pure-Go entry, it is complementary: rez is a SIMD resizer, go-images covers filters, colour and morphology and leaves resizing to go-gfx.
verified_claims_summary: Author-run parity table on an Apple M4 Max (macOS 26.5), go1.26.4 with go test -cpu=1 -count=5 against scikit-image 0.26.0/scipy 1.18.0 and OpenCV 4.13.0 pinned to one thread: RGB to HSV 65 vs 13.7 Mpix/s (4.7-4.8x) and box blur r=2 1.8-2.6x over scikit-image, but the scikit-image side runs float64 in and float64 out while go-images and OpenCV run uint8, and OpenCV is 15-30x faster than go-images on those same rows. The code review adds measurement caveats in both directions: morphology rows, labelled '(gray)' by aggregate.py, time go-images on three RGB channels of a random colour image against scikit-image and OpenCV on one uint8 gray plane (so its losses there are overstated), Gaussian is 3-sigma vs 4-sigma, and the HSV numbers (BENCHMARKS.md last edited 2026-07-02) predate the 2026-08-15 move of the HSV kernel onto go-gfx/color, which was not re-timed in the published table.
status_note: Active (37 commits from 2026-06-15 to 2026-09-27, mostly feature work and go-gfx dependency bumps), BSD-3-Clause and pure Go so it is easy to vendor, but it has one star, no releases and no outside users or issue reports yet.
